Lockheed Martin.blurb: Lockheed Martin is the largest U.S. defense contractor and a central supplier in Foreign Military Sales, spanning fighters, missiles, rotary-wing aircraft, and C4ISR. Its platforms underpin many allied air forces and missile-defense architectures.

The Boeing Company.blurb: Boeing is a major U.S. aerospace and defense prime whose military portfolio includes fighters, airlift, tankers, rotorcraft, and munitions. Through FMS it remains one of the principal sources of U.S. combat aircraft and support fleets for partner nations.

RTX Corporation.blurb: RTX (formerly Raytheon Technologies) is a leading U.S. missiles, sensors, and aerospace systems company. Its air-defense, air-to-air, and precision-strike products are among the most widely transferred U.S. capabilities under Foreign Military Sales.

Northrop Grumman.blurb: Northrop Grumman is a major U.S. defense contractor focused on autonomous systems, airborne early warning, space, and advanced electronics. In FMS it often appears as the supplier for surveillance aircraft, unmanned systems, and mission electronics.

General Dynamics.blurb: General Dynamics is a diversified U.S. defense contractor covering land combat vehicles, naval systems, munitions, and IT services. Its armored vehicles and related support packages are a recurring element of U.S. ground-force transfers abroad.

BAE Systems.blurb: BAE Systems is a major UK-based defense contractor with a large U.S. footprint in combat vehicles, electronics, and naval systems. Through its American subsidiaries it frequently appears as a prime or teammate on FMS vehicle and electronics programs.

L3Harris Technologies.blurb: L3Harris Technologies is a U.S. defense electronics company specializing in communications, ISR, avionics, and electronic warfare. It commonly supplies radios, sensors, and mission systems that integrate into broader FMS platform packages.

General Atomics.blurb: General Atomics is best known for long-endurance remotely piloted aircraft and related sensors used for ISR and strike. Its MQ-series systems are among the most visible unmanned platforms transferred through U.S. security cooperation channels.

Sikorsky Aircraft.blurb: Sikorsky, a Lockheed Martin company, builds military helicopters used for assault, utility, and maritime missions. Black Hawk–family and Seahawk aircraft are staples of U.S. rotary-wing Foreign Military Sales.

Longbow LLC.blurb: Longbow LLC is a Lockheed Martin–Northrop Grumman joint venture that builds the AN/APG-78 Longbow fire-control radar for the AH-64 Apache. In Foreign Military Sales it appears almost exclusively on Apache packages that include the mast-mounted radar and related Hellfire Longbow components.

Hellfire Systems LLC.blurb: Hellfire Systems LLC is the Lockheed Martin–Boeing joint venture that produces AGM-114 Hellfire missiles. It is the recurring prime contractor on Hellfire Foreign Military Sales cases and related missile support packages.

Javelin Joint Venture.blurb: The Javelin Joint Venture is a Lockheed Martin–RTX (Raytheon) consortium that builds the FGM-148 Javelin anti-armor missile. It is the standard prime on Javelin Foreign Military Sales cases, covering missiles, launch units, and related training and support.

Pratt & Whitney.blurb: Pratt & Whitney is an RTX company and a leading maker of military aircraft engines. Its powerplants equip many U.S. fighters and trainers sold abroad, making engine support a recurring line in FMS sustainment packages.

GE Aerospace.blurb: GE Aerospace produces military aircraft engines and related propulsion systems for fighters, helicopters, and airlifters. Engine sales and follow-on support frequently travel with U.S. aircraft packages under Foreign Military Sales.

Collins Aerospace.blurb: Collins Aerospace, an RTX company, supplies avionics, cabin systems, and mission electronics for military aircraft. In FMS notifications it often appears as a systems or components supplier within larger platform sales.

Bell Textron.blurb: Bell Textron builds military helicopters and tiltrotors used for attack, utility, and assault support. Its rotorcraft and related training or support packages recur across U.S. aviation Foreign Military Sales.

Textron Inc..blurb: Textron is a diversified U.S. industrial company whose defense brands include aviation, unmanned systems, and specialty vehicles. Through subsidiaries it supplies trainers, light aircraft, and other niche platforms into FMS cases.

Honeywell International.blurb: Honeywell supplies aerospace systems, engines, and avionics used across military aircraft fleets. In Foreign Military Sales it typically appears as a propulsion or systems provider tied to larger platform programs.

AM General.blurb: AM General is the long-time manufacturer of the Humvee and related light tactical vehicles. Its wheeled platforms and spare-parts support have been a durable staple of U.S. ground-vehicle transfers abroad.

Leonardo DRS.blurb: Leonardo DRS is the U.S. defense arm of Leonardo, focused on electro-optics, computing, and force-protection systems. It supplies sensors and electronic subsystems that integrate into broader U.S. platform and vehicle sales.

Rolls-Royce.blurb: Rolls-Royce is a major aero-engine manufacturer whose military engines power helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft in U.S. and allied fleets. Engine supply and logistics support appear in FMS cases tied to those platforms.

Leidos.blurb: Leidos is a U.S. science and technology contractor spanning defense IT, intelligence, and mission support. On FMS pages it typically appears in systems integration, training, or program-support roles rather than as a platform OEM.

Booz Allen Hamilton.blurb: Booz Allen Hamilton is a major U.S. consulting and technology firm with deep defense and intelligence work. In Foreign Military Sales it appears infrequently, usually in engineering services or program-support roles alongside platform primes.

Anduril Industries.blurb: Anduril Industries develops autonomous systems, counter-UAS, and software-defined sensing for U.S. and allied forces. In Foreign Military Sales it appears as a supplier of networked unmanned and air-defense capabilities for partners modernizing tactical awareness and force protection.

Navistar Defense.blurb: Navistar Defense supplies medium and heavy tactical trucks used for logistics and mobility. Its commercial-derived military vehicles and parts support appear in ground-force Foreign Military Sales packages.

CAE Inc..blurb: CAE is a Canadian simulation and training company with a large U.S. defense presence. It supplies flight simulators and training systems that often accompany aircraft Foreign Military Sales as aircrew and maintainer pipelines.

FLIR Systems.blurb: FLIR (now part of Teledyne) is known for infrared cameras and electro-optical sensors used in surveillance, targeting, and force protection. Those sensors frequently travel as components within larger U.S. FMS equipment packages.

Elbit Systems.blurb: Elbit Systems is an Israeli defense electronics company with substantial U.S. operations in avionics, munitions, and soldier systems. It appears in FMS when U.S.-sourced cases include Elbit-built components or U.S. subsidiary work.

Thales Group.blurb: Thales is a European defense and aerospace electronics group with U.S. subsidiaries in communications, sensors, and avionics. In American FMS notifications it typically shows up as a systems or electronics teammate on multinational programs.

Airbus.blurb: Airbus is a European aerospace manufacturer whose defense and helicopter lines serve many allied militaries. U.S. FMS involvement is selective, often tied to specific platforms, components, or U.S.-based support work.

V2X Inc..blurb: V2X (formerly Vectrus and related mission-support businesses) provides base operations, logistics, and training support for U.S. and partner forces. In FMS it appears as a services contractor rather than a weapons manufacturer.

KBR Inc..blurb: KBR is a U.S. engineering and government-services company with long-running defense logistics and base-support work. When it appears in FMS material, it is usually for sustainment, training, or program services around equipment sales.

Kaman Corporation.blurb: Kaman Corporation is a U.S. aerospace and defense company known for naval helicopters and precision fuzes, including the Joint Programmable Fuze used with JDAM and Paveway munitions. In FMS it appears on rotary-wing packages and as a teammate on air-delivered ammunition cases.

SAIC.blurb: SAIC is a U.S. technology and engineering services contractor supporting defense IT, training, and systems integration. Its FMS footprint is typically advisory or sustainment-oriented rather than platform production.

Moog Inc..blurb: Moog supplies precision motion-control and actuation systems used in aircraft, missiles, and space vehicles. In Foreign Military Sales it usually appears as a critical components supplier within larger prime-contractor packages.

Aerojet Rocketdyne.blurb: Aerojet Rocketdyne builds rocket motors and propulsion systems for missiles and spacecraft. Its motors are embedded in many U.S. munitions and space-launch products that can travel with FMS missile and propulsion cases.

BWX Technologies.blurb: BWX Technologies specializes in nuclear components and related engineering for naval propulsion and national-security applications. Its FMS appearances are rare and usually tied to specialized technical or support work.

Draper Laboratory.blurb: Draper is a U.S. nonprofit engineering lab known for guidance, navigation, and control systems. In defense transfers it typically contributes specialized guidance technology rather than complete weapon platforms.

Maxar Technologies.blurb: Maxar is a U.S. space and geospatial intelligence company providing satellite imagery and related analytics. When it surfaces in security-cooperation contexts, it is usually for ISR data or space-based sensing support.

Colt's Manufacturing.blurb: Colt is a historic U.S. small-arms manufacturer whose rifles and related weapons have long equipped American and partner forces. In FMS it appears mainly in infantry-weapons and spare-parts cases.

SRC Inc..blurb: SRC is a U.S. nonprofit research and development company focused on radar, electronic warfare, and related sensors. It occasionally appears in FMS as a technology or systems provider for specialized electronic missions.

Gulfstream Aerospace.blurb: Gulfstream builds business jets that are often converted into special-mission or VIP transport aircraft for partner governments. Those aircraft and related support packages occasionally move through U.S. Foreign Military Sales channels.

Viasat Inc..blurb: Viasat provides military satellite communications and networking equipment used to connect forces beyond line of sight. In FMS it typically appears as a communications or terminal supplier within larger C4ISR packages.

Aero Vironment.blurb: Aero Vironment builds small unmanned aircraft and loitering munitions used for tactical ISR and strike. Its portable drone systems are a recurring category in U.S. security assistance for partner ground forces.

Zone 5 Technologies.blurb: Zone 5 Technologies is a California-based U.S. missile and unmanned systems company focused on affordable, mass-producible strike munitions. It is a principal contractor on the Extended Range Attack Munition (ERAM) program, including the major Ukraine FMS case.

CoAspire.blurb: CoAspire is a U.S. defense contractor developing affordable air-launched cruise missiles, including the RAACM family. Alongside Zone 5 Technologies, it is a principal contractor for Extended Range Attack Munition (ERAM) Foreign Military Sales.

Allison Transmission.blurb: Allison Transmission is a U.S. propulsion company that builds automatic and cross-drive transmissions for wheeled and tracked military vehicles. In Foreign Military Sales it typically appears as a drivetrain supplier within armored-vehicle and tactical-truck packages.

Kratos Defense & Security Solutions.blurb: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions builds unmanned aircraft, rocket systems, and C5ISR products for U.S. and allied customers. It often appears in FMS as a supplier of drones, targets, or specialized mission systems.

Beechcraft Defense.blurb: Beechcraft, part of Textron Aviation, builds military trainers and special-mission aircraft such as the T-6 Texan II family. It appears in FMS mainly as the airframe prime for training and light attack or ISR derivatives sold to partner air forces.

Oshkosh Defense.blurb: Oshkosh Defense builds tactical wheeled vehicles, including JLTV and heavy trucks used by U.S. and partner ground forces. Vehicle fleets and sustainment kits make it a frequent name in land-system Foreign Military Sales.

Sierra Nevada Corporation.blurb: Sierra Nevada Corporation is a U.S. aerospace and defense company known for aircraft modernization, ISR platforms, and space systems. In FMS it commonly supports special-mission aircraft and related integration work.

Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace.blurb: Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace is a Norwegian defense company known for naval strike missiles and remote weapon stations. It appears in U.S. FMS when American cases include Kongsberg systems produced or integrated for partner nations.

Huntington Ingalls Industries.blurb: HII (Huntington Ingalls Industries) is America’s largest military shipbuilder, constructing aircraft carriers, amphibious ships, and surface combatants. In FMS it more often appears through ship systems, support, or specialized naval work than full hull transfers.

Vinnell Arabia.blurb: Vinnell Arabia is a U.S.-linked training and support contractor long associated with Saudi Arabian military modernization programs. It appears in FMS material mainly as a services and training provider rather than an equipment OEM.

Marvin Group.blurb: The Marvin Group is a Southern California aerospace and defense manufacturer whose flagship unit, Marvin Engineering, builds stores carriage and release gear and other alternate mission equipment for fighters, helicopters, and UAS. It commonly appears in FMS as a teammate supplying aircraft armament and auxiliary equipment alongside the primes.

Progeny Systems.blurb: Progeny Systems is a General Dynamics Mission Systems business focused on naval combat systems, acoustics, torpedo guidance and control, cybersecurity, and related electronics for U.S. and allied submarines and surface ships. In Foreign Military Sales it typically appears on undersea-warfare and naval combat-system packages alongside other U.S. naval primes.

Toyota.blurb: Toyota Motor North America (Plano, Texas) appears in State Department Foreign Military Sales notices as a commercial vehicle supplier. Its cases typically cover trucks and related ground mobility for partner security and border programs rather than traditional combat platforms.

AAR Corporation.blurb: AAR Corporation is a U.S. aerospace and defense logistics company that supplies aircraft maintenance, mobility systems, and specialty manufacturing. In Foreign Military Sales it often appears through its AAR Manufacturing unit (Cadillac, MI) on vehicle chassis and related ground-support packages.

Cobham Defense Electronics.blurb: Cobham Defense Electronics is a UK-origin aerospace and defense electronics company whose U.S. businesses supply airborne connectivity, radios, and related mission electronics. In Foreign Military Sales it appears as a specialty electronics prime or teammate on communications and aircraft-systems packages.

AgustaWestland.blurb: AgustaWestland (Leonardo Helicopters) builds commercial and military rotorcraft, including the AW119 family. Through its Philadelphia operations it is a recurring FMS supplier of light utility helicopters and related support for partner nations.

Caterpillar.blurb: Caterpillar is a U.S. heavy-equipment manufacturer whose defense-relevant products include armored combat bulldozers and related earthmoving systems. In Foreign Military Sales it appears as the prime on D9 and similar engineering-vehicle packages for partner ground forces.

American Ordnance.blurb: American Ordnance is a U.S. munitions manufacturer and Day & Zimmermann company that operates the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. It load-assembles medium- and large-caliber ammunition and appears in FMS as a prime on artillery-projectile and related ordnance packages.

Orbital ATK.blurb: Orbital ATK was a U.S. aerospace and defense company formed from Orbital Sciences and Alliant Techsystems, known for munitions, missile components, and precision-guidance kits. It appears in FMS chiefly on ammunition and weapons packages; Northrop Grumman acquired it in 2018.

GC Micro.blurb: GC Micro is a U.S. technology integrator and value-added reseller that supplies hardware, software, and configured systems to government, defense, and aerospace customers. In Foreign Military Sales it typically appears as a specialty electronics or IT teammate inside larger platform packages.

Spirit Aero.blurb: Spirit AeroSystems is a major aerostructures manufacturer that builds fuselage, wing, and related assemblies for commercial and military aircraft. In FMS notifications it often appears as a structures teammate on helicopter and fixed-wing packages; Boeing completed its acquisition in late 2025.

Telephonics.blurb: Telephonics is a U.S. aerospace and defense electronics company known for surveillance radars, IFF, and maritime/airborne mission systems. It commonly appears in FMS as a sensors and communications supplier within broader aircraft packages, including Black Hawk-related cases.

Pole Zero.blurb: Pole/Zero (an MPG / Dover Microwave Products Group brand) builds RF and microwave filters and related communications-protection gear. In Foreign Military Sales it appears as a specialty RF teammate on avionics and electronic-warfare packages rather than as a platform prime.

Terma.blurb: Terma is a Danish aerospace and defense company that supplies aircraft self-protection, aerostructures, radars, and mission electronics. In U.S. FMS cases it often appears as a teammate providing aircraft survivability equipment and related structures on helicopter and fighter packages.

Symmetrics.blurb: Symetrics Industries (now Extant Aerospace) manufactures and sustains aerospace electronics, including electronic-warfare and data-modem products used on military aircraft. In FMS it typically appears as an avionics or EW teammate on rotary-wing and fixed-wing packages.

Arnprior Aerospace.blurb: Arnprior Aerospace is a Canadian aerostructures manufacturer that designs and builds mechanical structures and assemblies for aerospace and defense customers. In Foreign Military Sales it appears as a structures teammate on aircraft packages rather than as the platform prime.

Martin Baker.blurb: Martin-Baker is a UK aircrew-safety company and the world’s leading maker of ejection seats and crashworthy crew seats. In FMS notifications it commonly supplies crashworthy seats and related safety equipment for helicopters such as the UH-60 Black Hawk.
